previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain following a five-day polysubstance binge involving alcohol, cocaine, and heroin. He had a high blood alcohol level and positive urine toxicology for opioids. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal troponins and unchanged EKG. The chest pain was deemed atypical and likely related to alcohol and opioid withdrawal, though hypertension may have contributed. He was treated with Valium for withdrawal, restarted on lisinopril and other cardiac medications, and started on Imdur for blood pressure. Metoprolol was held due to recent cocaine use. The patient decided to leave against medical advice after being counseled on the risks. He was provided with rehab resources and instructed to follow up with his primary care physician.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with history of CAD s/p PCI RCA, LCX, LAD, 
and OM, COPD, and polysubstance abuse who presents with chest 
pain following recent admission for pneumonia to ___ 
___ and found to be in alcohol withdrawal.
.
#Alcohol withdrawal: The patient reported a history of heavy 
ETOH use. He was noted to be in alcohol withdrawal on admission 
to the ED with symptoms including confusion, tachycardia, and 
tremulousness. As above he received benzodiazepines in the ED 
and was started on CIWA scale with PRN diazepam.  The patient 
was also given thiamine, folate and a multivitamin. The morning 
following admission he unfortunately ultimately decided to leave 
AMA. The risks of withdrawal including seizure and death were 
explained. He vocalized understanding of these risks and still 
decided to leave against medical advice. 
.
#Pneumonia: The patient is mildly dyspneic at rest, with dyspnea 
on minimal exertion (steps) without hypoxia. He was treated 
recently for CAP at ___, but did not complete his course 
due to elopement. CXR here did not show evidence of PNA despite 
continued cough. ACS was felt to be unlikely in the absence of 
acute EKG changes or troponinemia, as is PE in the absence of 
hypoxia. Although he is known to have systolic HF and an echo 
showed worsened systolic function, there was no evidence of 
decompensation on exam, and no evidence of pulmonary edema on 
CXR. He was initially started on vancomycin and cefepime to 
cover for a HCAP.  As above he ultimately decided to leave 
against medical attention. On leaving he was provided with a 
prescription to complete a course of levofloxacin given report 
of untreated PNA at ___. 
.
#Chest pain: On admission the patient reported substernal chest 
pain in the setting of significant CAD history without acute EKG 
changes or troponinemia, arguing against ACS. Although he 
reports improvement with leaning forward, there are no EKG 
changes to suggest pericarditis. There is no pleuritic component 
or hypoxia, making PE less likely. Chest pain improved without 
intervention prior to discharge. 
.
#Afib with RVR: Patient was noted to have new afib. On review of 
OMR, there is no prior documentation of afib. Tachycardia is 
confounded by presence of infection and alcohol withdrawal. 
Trigger is unclear, but may reflect underlying infection 
(pneumonia). New ischemic event unlikely in the absence of acute 
ischemic EKG changes or troponinemia.  CHADS score of 2, hence 
anticoagulation indicated if afib persistent, though he is a 
poor candidate, given serial noncompliance. As above repeat echo 
did show worsened systolic function. HR improved with treatment 
of withdrawal and hydration. These results were explained to the 
patient. Unfortunately he did not stay for further evaluation.   

.
#CAD: He has an extensive CAD history, including multiple 
stents. He is not compliant with his medications at home. There 
are no acute ischemic EKG changes or cardiac enzyme elevations 
to suggest an acute event. He was resumed on home aspirin 325mg 
daily and lisinopril at 5mg daily. Would strongly consider 
initiation of a beta blocker as an outpatient however would need 
to weigh the risk of beta blockade in the setting of cocaine 
use. 

#.Systolic HF: LVEF of 35% on cardiac stress echo in ___. 
There are no signs of decompensated heart failure on admission. 
As above his home aspirin and lisinopril were restarted. Beta 
blockage were held given ongoing cocaine use.  Echo demonstrated 
EF of 25 to 30%. 
.
Transitional Issues
Patient was full code throughout this hospitalization 
Patient was encouraged to follow-up with his PCP regarding heart 
failure, new afib and pneumonia. Would consider initiation of 
rate control agents.
